newsitem.title: RWANDA: Rwanda orders expulsion of Reuters correspondent.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda orders expulsion of Reuters correspondent.

text.p: Rwanda's interior ministry ordered the expulsion of Reuters correspondent Christian Jennings on Sunday.

Jennings said two ministry officials served him with a deportation order saying his presence in the country was undesirable. The officials told him to leave within 24 hours but the written order gave no deadline.
Reuters editor-in-chief Mark Wood said: "We are surprised by this decision and concerned. We plan to be in contact with the government of Rwanda to ask for a full explanation and to seek a review."

Jennings, a 34-year-old Briton, has been based in Rwanda since August 1996 as a freelance correspondent working for Reuters. He has reported from Rwanda and neighbouring Zaire on the rebellion which began there last October.
Jennings has a valid Rwandan visa and press accreditation issued by the ministry of information.
Official Rwandan and foreign diplomatic sources said a February 7 Reuters report about a news conference in Kigali given by Vice-President Paul Kagame led to the expulsion order.

The report quoted Kagame as saying Rwanda had the right to divert some foreign aid to help the internal war against Hutu extremists because security was the priority for both the Rwandan government and foreign donors.
